transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20 11:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood, AE)
- Arjun Patel (Redwood, SE)
- Liam O'Neill (Redwood, CSM)
- Sara Gomez (Luminate, Head of ML)
- Tom Rivera (Luminate, CTO)
- Priya Shah (Luminate, Platform Eng)
- Evan Li (Luminate, Data Ops)

Summary: QBR style check-in. Usage has increased 48% quarter-over-quarter, cost trending up due to higher long-context LLM usage and more frequent embeddings for search. Discussed reliability incident on 2026-04-12 where latency spiked during promo event; dug into autoscaling and model routing fallbacks. Talked through Dedicated sizing and SOC2 + SAML timeline. Agreed on next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time for the QBR. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Sara Gomez: Hi all, Sara here.
[00:14] Tom Rivera: Tom here.
[00:16] Priya Shah: Priya.
[00:18] Evan Li: Evan.
[00:20] Arjun Patel: Arjun from Redwood.
[00:22] Liam O'Neill: Liam, CS.
[00:24] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda — quick usage overview, cost drivers, reliability incident walkthrough, roadmap (dedicated/private timing), security/compliance items, and wrap with next steps.

[02:00] Maya Chen: Sara, before we jump in, are there any specific goals you want to make sure we hit in the QBR?
[02:07] Sara Gomez: Yeah, main thing is we need a clear plan to keep latency under 180ms p99 for user-facing chat and knock down cost per session. Also we have the SOC2 audit coming up mid-July, so we need artifacts and a clear timeline for SAML and audit logs.
[02:25] Tom Rivera: And for us infra-wise, we're looking at Dedicated if it gives predictable throughput and better isolation; but we also need to see cost delta vs hosted.

[04:00] Arjun Patel: Cool. I'll jump into the usage trends — we pulled your last 90 days. We see a 48% qtr-on-qtr increase in token volume, biggest driver is longer context prompts for our recommendation flows, and a 30% uptick in embeddings calls for semantic search. Peak QPS during the April promo hit about 240 reqs/sec which is where you saw the latency spike.
[04:22] Priya Shah: That matches our logs; we had a burst across three regions but mostly us-west. Latency went from ~75ms to 450ms p95 at the worst.
[04:35] Arjun Patel: Right, and that triggered autoscale but the cold-starts and model fallback to a larger variant created extra latency. We also noticed your KV cache hit rate was low — looks like prefix caching isn't being leveraged as much in the recommendation path.
[04:52] Evan Li: The KV cache? In our telemetry it's labelled K V cash sometimes in the logs haha, there's some obfuscation in our parser.

[06:00] Maya Chen: On costs — here's the quick callout: longer contexts + embeddings are the two big drivers. We modeled an optimization path: batching and prefix caching can drop per-token infra cost by ~22%, switching to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical backfill jobs could save another ~15%. For interactive chat we recommend keeping the higher-precision model.
[06:30] Sara Gomez: That sounds reasonable. We are worried about quality regressions with quantization — can we get suggestions per workload?
[06:42] Arjun Patel: Absolutely, we can provide quantization recommendations by workload. We'll run a small eval against your prompt set — Redwood Optimize can surface where 4-bit is acceptable and where we should stick to FP16. We'll include regression thresholds.

[08:00] Tom Rivera: On Dedicated — what's the timeline and constraints? We need SLA and probably a private VPC setup.
[08:10] Liam O'Neill: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts; provisioning lead time is typically 2-4 weeks once sizing is agreed and networking is validated. VPC peering, SAML, and KMS integration all add to the checklist. We can align on a pilot-sized pool first.
[08:28] Priya Shah: What's the expected cost premium for Dedicated vs hosted? Ballpark.
[08:33] Maya Chen: Ballpark depends on commit and instance type — with a 3-month commit you can get a 10-20% discount off pure pay-as-you-go hosted, plus you'll get more predictable unit economics and better latency stability. We'll send a detailed scenario for your current usage.

[10:00] Sara Gomez: Can you walk us through the reliability incident on 2026-04-12? We want to understand root cause and mitigation.
[10:10] Arjun Patel: Sure — timeline: at 14:03 PT we saw a sudden increase in long-context generation jobs. Our routing policy attempted to spread across available pools, but a burst caused auto-batcher backlogs and one worker pool hit memory pressure; the runtime performed fallback to a cheaper variant which had slightly different KV cache layout causing repeated cache misses. That, plus worker restart churn, produced the latency spike.
[10:44] Sara Gomez: So cache misses + fallback + restarts, got it. How do we prevent that?
[10:49] Arjun Patel: Short term: increase autoscale headroom for that route, enable pre-warming for known promo windows, and enable prefix caching for recommendation pipeline. Mid-term: move that route to a Dedicated pool with reserved headroom or configure reserved burst capacity.

[12:00] Priya Shah: Pre-warming — is that manual or can Redwood schedule it?
[12:06] Maya Chen: We can schedule pre-warms or provide APIs for you to trigger pre-warm jobs. We'll include a runbook for promo window pre-warm and suggested thresholds.

[13:30] Tom Rivera: About security — SOC2 evidence, SAML, and audit logs are critical. We need an architecture diagram showing where audit logs live and KMS key ownership.
[13:40] Liam O'Neill: We'll share the SOC2 artifacts and an integration diagram. For Private/Dedicated deployments, customers can retain KMS control; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options. SAML SSO is supported — we'll send the SAML metadata and a short guide.
[14:05] Sara Gomez: Great. Also asking about data retention for embeddings — can we configure shorter retention for derived embeddings?
[14:12] Arjun Patel: Yes — embedding retention policies are configurable per project; we'll include recommended defaults and a sample config for your environment.

[16:00] Maya Chen: One thing customers ask is about vendor lock and fallback — if Dedicated saturates, what's the graceful degradation?
[16:08] Arjun Patel: You can configure smart routing policies — failover to hosted models in another region or a lower-cost variant. We try to preserve correctness by routing to compatible model variants and returning a deprecation notice in headers.

[18:00] Evan Li: Any integrations for our observability stack? We want traces and token-level cost breakdowns in our dashboard.
[18:08] Liam O'Neill: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. We also have tracing hooks that export to OTLP and can integrate with your existing Grafana/Datadog setup. We'll share the export examples.

[20:00] Priya Shah: For the pilot sizing, what inputs do you need from us?
[20:06] Arjun Patel: 30 days token usage, peak QPS, expected growth rates, acceptable p99 latency SLO, and which routes are critical. Plus any compliance constraints.
[20:18] Priya Shah: We'll get that to you. I'll attach the CSV and a short notes file.

[22:00] Maya Chen: Let's talk pricing scenarios quickly — baseline hosted cost, hosted with batching/prefix caching, and Dedicated with a 3-month commit. We'll run numbers and show projected savings and latency impact.
[22:20] Sara Gomez: Important to show quality delta if we apply quantization for backfill.
[22:25] Arjun Patel: We'll include evaluation results vs your prompt set — Redwood Optimize will flag regressions and recommend which workloads are safe for 4-bit or int8.

[24:00] Tom Rivera: Competitor question: we've looked at MegaCloud AI's managed endpoints — they offer deeper network egress discounts but their latency was inconsistent in prior tests. How do you compare?
[24:15] Maya Chen: We see customers migrate when predictable inference economics and routing flexibility matter. We'll include a short competitive note but the concrete is the benchmark with your workload. We'll run a side-by-side for your key routes if you'd like.

[26:00] Sara Gomez: On SLAs — if we move to Dedicated, what uptime/latency SLAs are available?
[26:08] Liam O'Neill: Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts. We'll scope that when you move forward.

[28:00] Priya Shah: A note on networking — we need to validate VPC peering and egress rules. Are there standard firewall rules?
[28:10] Arjun Patel: Yes, we'll provide the VPC peering checklist and sample security group rules. Also note that for on-prem/private deployments there are additional steps; we'll include the matrix in the docs.

[30:00] Maya Chen: Recap of actions — Redwood sends pricing and pilot proposal, SOC2 docs, SAML metadata, and a Dedicated sizing draft. Luminate shares usage CSV and identifies promo windows.

[31:20] Sara Gomez: One question — can you commit to a pilot start date? We ideally want a pilot in June to be ready before our July audit for SOC2 artifacts.
[31:30] Maya Chen: We can target a pilot kick-off the week of 2026-06-14 pending sign-off. We'll surface the exact timeline in the proposal.

[33:00] Tom Rivera: Anything else on the roadmap? We're planning to move more of the recommendation traffic to the LLM path in Q3. If we do that, we'll need a re-evaluation of Dedicated sizing.
[33:12] Arjun Patel: Noted — we'll model Q3 growth scenarios and give a recommended scale path.

[35:00] Evan Li: Small note — our telemetry has inconsistent naming for Redis and KV layers; we'll clean that up before sharing logs.
[35:08] Priya Shah: We'll try to provide the cleaned CSV.

[38:00] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the proposal and docs.

[39:00] Liam O'Neill: I'll drop SOC2 checklist and the SAML guide after this call.

[40:00] Sara Gomez: Thanks.

[40:10] Tom Rivera: Thanks all.

[40:20] Priya Shah: Bye.

[40:30] Maya Chen: End of recording.
notes: Transcript contains some transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache). References to Redwood products: Redwood Optimize, Redwood Console, Dedicated. Customer requested SOC2 artifacts and SAML metadata. Agreed pilot timeline week of 2026-06-14.
